profiles.name: Truda Marson
profiles.excerpt: Truda Marson was a recurring Lux Radio Theatre supporting actress whose thirty-six sponsor-facing credits make commercial presentation a substantial part of her preserved radio record.
profiles.bio_html:
Truda Marson is best documented through the production record of West Coast network radio rather than through a large surviving body of personal publicity. Her GRH credits place her most often on Lux Radio Theatre, where supporting actors worked around major film stars in a demanding weekly adaptation schedule.

Marson’s Lux entries repeatedly combine performer and commercial-spokesman roles. The volume makes this more than an incidental sponsor appearance and shows the way experienced studio actors could be integrated directly into the advertising that financed the drama.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 36 Lux Radio Theatre sponsor/performer credits, four Broadway Is My Beat performances and a The Whistler appearance. GRH keeps the biography centered on that verified broadcast work while leaving unsupported personal details out.

profiles.name: Tyler McVey
profiles.excerpt: Tyler McVey built a broad character-acting career in radio before television, with Lux Radio Theatre repeatedly using him in both supporting roles and sponsor presentation.
profiles.bio_html:
William Tyler McVey began acting in amateur productions while still a student in Michigan and built professional experience in radio before becoming a familiar film and television character actor. His mature screen career often cast him as officials, doctors and authority figures, roles well suited to the controlled vocal presence radio had already developed.

GRH preserves McVey across westerns, comedy, detective drama and prestige anthology. Lux Radio Theatre is a major part of that record and repeatedly tags him in commercial-spokesman as well as performer roles, showing another side of the practical studio work behind the weekly Hollywood adaptations.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 24 Lux Radio Theatre sponsor/performer credits, 18 Wild Bill Hickok performances, ten Fibber McGee and Molly appearances and additional work on Sears Radio Theater, Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar, Roy Rogers and other programs.

profiles.name: Betty Moran
profiles.excerpt: Betty Moran was a West Coast radio actress heard across Night Beat, Screen Directors Playhouse and detective drama, with a smaller but repeated sponsor-facing role on Lux Radio Theatre.
profiles.bio_html:
Betty Moran appears in the GRH archive as a working West Coast repertory actress rather than a performer tied to one signature character. Her credits move through Night Beat, Screen Directors Playhouse, Richard Diamond, Tales of the Texas Rangers and Let George Do It.

Her Lux Radio Theatre records also include commercial-spokesman tags. The sponsor work is much smaller than her dramatic record, but it occurs on more than one preserved broadcast and is retained as a secondary facet rather than allowed to redefine her primary identity.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves seven Night Beat performances, five Screen Directors Playhouse appearances, three each on Richard Diamond and Tales of the Texas Rangers, and two Lux Radio Theatre sponsor/performer credits.

profiles.name: Jane Morgan
profiles.excerpt: Jane Morgan spent decades moving from vaudeville and stage work into radio, becoming best known as Mrs. Davis on Our Miss Brooks while also serving regularly in Lux Radio Theatre’s studio and sponsor company.
profiles.bio_html:
Jane Morgan, born Jennie Morgan in England in 1880, had already spent decades in concert halls, vaudeville and legitimate theatre before radio became a central part of her career. She began broadcasting work in the 1930s and became one of the medium’s dependable mature character actresses.

Her defining later role was Mrs. Davis, Eve Arden’s well-meaning and eccentric landlady on Our Miss Brooks, a character Morgan carried into television. Before that long-running comedy success, she was a stock performer on Lux Radio Theatre, where GRH’s records also place her in sponsor presentation.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 23 Lux Radio Theatre commercial-spokesman/commercial-spokeswoman/performer credits, four The Great Gildersleeve performances and additional work on Encore Theater, A Man Called X, Boston Blackie, Broadway Is My Beat, Dr. Christian and Lights Out. GRH keeps her distinct from the later popular singer also named Jane Morgan.

profiles.name: Ann Morrison
profiles.excerpt: Ann Morrison was a West Coast repertory actress heard in Philip Marlowe, Gunsmoke and other major dramas, with additional sponsor-facing work on Lux Radio Theatre.
profiles.bio_html:
Ann Morrison appears across Golden Radio Hour as a working dramatic actress whose preserved credits span detective stories, westerns, small-town drama and prestige anthology. The variety matters because it places her inside the flexible Los Angeles repertory pool rather than around one continuing character.

Her GRH identity also corrects the duplicate source spelling “Anne Morrison,” which was carrying overlapping Escape material. The canonical Ann Morrison record includes Lux Radio Theatre commercial-spokesman tags, preserving sponsor work without creating a second person.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves seven Philip Marlowe performances, five Lux Radio Theatre sponsor/performer credits, four Gunsmoke appearances and additional work on Dr. Christian, Fort Laramie, Have Gun, Will Travel, Richard Diamond and Escape.

profiles.name: Janet Scott
profiles.excerpt: Janet Scott was one of Lux Radio Theatre’s regular studio voices, with twenty-seven preserved sponsor-and-performance credits plus appearances on other Hollywood radio anthologies.
profiles.bio_html:
Janet Scott’s radio record is dominated by Lux Radio Theatre, where the weekly adaptation format depended on a recurring group of professional voices around its celebrity guests. Her work belongs to the studio infrastructure that made the program sound polished even when the stars changed every week.

Scott’s GRH records repeatedly combine performer and commercial-spokesman roles. The same production could therefore use her both inside the fictional adaptation and in the sponsor presentation that surrounded it.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 27 Lux Radio Theatre sponsor/performer credits plus appearances on Screen Directors Playhouse, The Halls of Ivy, The Railroad Hour and Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar. Personal documentation remains limited, so GRH keeps the page focused on the substantial verified radio work.

profiles.name: Ynez Seabury
profiles.excerpt: Ynez Seabury grew from child actress of the silent-film era into stage and radio work, with Lux Radio Theatre preserving a later chapter that included sponsor presentation.
profiles.bio_html:
Ynez Seabury was born in Portland, Oregon, in 1907 to theatrical parents and entered films as a child, appearing for D. W. Griffith while still very young. Her career continued through stage work, Broadway and motion pictures into the sound era, giving her unusually deep professional experience before her radio appearances.

Golden Radio Hour preserves Seabury primarily through Lux Radio Theatre and Dr. Christian. Lux used her not only as a supporting performer but also in commercial-spokesman roles, part of the anthology’s practice of drawing members of the studio company into sponsor material.

GRH currently preserves 16 Lux Radio Theatre sponsor/performer credits and six Dr. Christian performances for Seabury. Her page therefore connects early film, stage and radio rather than presenting the sponsor work in isolation.

profiles.name: Sarah Selby
profiles.excerpt: Sarah Selby began in radio before becoming a familiar screen character actress, carrying a flexible mature voice through Lux sponsor work, The Whistler, Escape and later television.
profiles.bio_html:
Sarah Selby began professionally in radio and developed the character-actress range that later made her a familiar supporting presence in film and television. Her screen debut came as a voice in Disney’s Dumbo, and she later became known for recurring parts on programs such as Gunsmoke, Burns and Allen and Father Knows Best.

Radio had already trained that versatility. GRH preserves Selby across Lux Radio Theatre, The Whistler, Escape, Dragnet, Let George Do It and experimental anthologies. Her Lux credits repeatedly include commercial-spokesman tags, showing the familiar sponsored-radio crossover between character acting and advertising.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 12 Lux Radio Theatre sponsor/performer credits, 11 The Whistler performances, four Escape appearances and smaller holdings across several other series. GRH treats sponsor work as one verified facet of a broad character career.

profiles.name: Anne Stone
profiles.excerpt: Anne Stone was a recurring Lux Radio Theatre studio actress whose eleven sponsor-facing credits sat beside detective, police and adventure drama across West Coast radio.
profiles.bio_html:
Anne Stone is preserved in Golden Radio Hour as a working radio actress rather than a personality built around one continuing role. Her credits include detective and police drama as well as the large weekly adaptations mounted by Lux Radio Theatre.

At Lux, Stone’s records combine performer and commercial-spokeswoman roles. The repeated pattern places sponsor presentation among her documented skills rather than treating it as a stray one-time credit.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 11 Lux Radio Theatre sponsor/performer credits, two appearances each on Broadway Is My Beat and Philip Marlowe, and additional work on Dr. Kildare, The Line Up and Voyage of the Scarlet Queen. Reliable personal sources remain scarce, so GRH lets that broadcast record define the page.

profiles.name: Leora Thatcher
profiles.excerpt: Leora Thatcher brought years of stage repertory and teaching into radio serials, comedy and drama, with Lux Radio Theatre also using her in sponsor-facing work.
profiles.bio_html:
Leora Thatcher was born in Logan, Utah, in 1894 and studied speech and theatre before teaching and then joining professional repertory companies. She spent years with the Moroni Olsen Players and in long stage runs, including Tobacco Road, before radio and screen work broadened her career.

On radio Thatcher played continuing serial characters such as Marge Mulvaney on Lora Lawton and Mrs. Kramer on The Right to Happiness, while also appearing on comedy and anthology programs. GRH’s Lux records add commercial-spokesman work to that acting history.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves seven Lux Radio Theatre sponsor/performer credits, three Quiet Please performances, two Mel Blanc Show appearances and additional work on The Whistler and Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar. GRH treats the sponsor work as a secondary craft inside a much longer stage-and-radio career.
